（印：E.D. 2793 Date 24/11/31 Special Branch S.5. SECRET）
Date November 24, 1931.

Subject (in full) Incorrect report etc. in "Shanghai Nichi-Nichi Shimbun"

Made by □□□ Forwarded by C.D.I. J.W. Simpson.

Sir,

With reference to the attached I called upon
Mr. Yamamoto, Editor of the "Shanghai Nichi-Nichi Shimbun"
and pointed out to him my views on the matter of his report
on the Ongjima incident, and requested him to consider the matter
with a view to publishing a correction. Subsequently on
November 21, 1931, a publication, as per translation attached,
appeared in the above newspaper. This being in no way a
correction of the original report of the incident, we approached
Mr. Yamamoto, who stated he could do nothing further
in the matter as Mr. Okajima objected to the publication of any
such statement, as per your note.

（签名：Jas Simpson）

（手写批注：）
by
Mr Okajima is a member of
the Committee of the Japanese Civic Association
and evidently an influential person in the
Japanese Community there and it would appear that
Mr. Yamamoto is afraid to offend him by publishing the
correction to his report. Jas W.S.
25/1

Correct Version of Incident

At about 1.15 a.m. on October 28, a Japanese
named Okajima, accompanied by two Japanese women,
whilst proceeding to his home on Point Road in a
hired motor car, via Tungchow Road, was stopped at
the corner of Tungchow and Point Roads by C.P.C.s
1319 and 2784 on duty in that vicinity, who informed
the chauffeur of the car that Point Road from Tungchow
Road to Chaoufoong Road was closed to traffic
owing to road excavation taking place. On the
chauffeur attempting to turn the car around, Mr.
Okajima left the vehicle and removed the barrier and
two red lamps to the side of the road and ordered
the Chauffeur to proceed which he refused to do.
On the policemen remonstrating with Mr. Okajima for
his action, he caught hold of the pistol lanyard of
C.P.C. 1319 who had to struggle to set himself free.
The car by this time had left the scene and the
policeman took Mr. Okajima to Harbin Road Police
Station to have the matter cleared up. On inquiries
being completed Mr. Okajima was allowed to go. There
is absolutely no truth in the statement that a Chinese
policemen pointed his pistol at Mr. Okajima.

CHINESE CONSTABLE LEVELS PISTOL AT JAPANESE AND TAKES
HIM TO POLICE STATION.

The Shanghai Nichi-Nichi publishes the following
reports-
As frequently reported already there are certained
Shanghai Municipal Police Chinese Constables, who allow
themselves to be overcame by ill feeling towards the
Japanese.
At 1. a.m. October 28, a Chinese constable No.1319
suddenly stopped Mr. Okajima of the Okajima paper factory
on point Road when returning home in a motor car and
demanded that he accompany him to t he Police station
owing to his having violated the traffic regulation. Mr.
Okajima explained to the Police Officer that he had not
violated any traffic regulation but the former insisted on
his coming to Police station. Consequently Mr. Okajima
followed the Policeman to the corner of Urga and Hailar
Roads when another Chinese constable No. 2784, without
ascertaining the circumstances of the case, took off his
great coat and levelled his pitsol at Mr. Okajima saying
"Japanese are bad".
Subsequently Mr. Okajima requested policeman No.2784
to also come along to Police station where he demanded that
severe punishment be given to him.
Mr. Okajima did not violate any traffic regulation
and it seems that t he trouble was simply due to ill
feeling against the Japanese.

D. O. "D"

For report.

《上海日日新闻》刊登以下报道——
正如此前经常报道的那样，某些
上海公共租界工部局警务处的中国巡捕，任由自己
被对日本人的恶感所支配。
10月28日凌晨1点，中国巡捕1319号
突然在百老汇路上拦住了冈岛纸厂的冈岛先生，当时他正乘车回家，并以违反交通法规为由
要求他陪同前往捕房。冈岛先生向警官解释说他并未
违反任何交通法规，但前者坚持要他去捕房。因此，冈岛先生
跟随警察来到峨嵋路与海拉尔路路口，此时另一名中国巡捕2784号，在未查明
案件情况的情况下，脱下大衣，用枪指着冈岛先生，说道
“日本人很坏”。
随后，冈岛先生要求巡捕2784号
也一同前往捕房，并在那里要求对他予以严厉惩罚。
冈岛先生并未违反任何交通法规，此次纠纷似乎仅仅是由于
对日本人的恶感所致。

The following is the statement of C.P.C. 1319.
native of Anhwei. taken by me C.3.I. Ku.
at 8.30 a.m. on the 31/10/31. and interpreted by Clerk Huang.

I was on night duty, walking No.11 Beat with C.P.C. 2784 on Oct. 27th, 1931. At 1.15 a.m. the 28th, whilst on duty at corner of Point and Tungchow Roads, we saw a public motor-car Lic. No. 18115, driven by a Chinese and occupied by a Japanese, coming from the South along Tungchow Road and attempting to turn East into Point Road, which was at the time closed for all vehicular traffic, owing to the road-repairs, by placing across the road P.W.D. tressels attached with lighted warning lamps. The Japanese occupier, seeing his car being thus stopped, came out of the motor car, and, removing tressels to the side of road, ordered the driver to proceed along. I rushed up with C.P.C. 2784 and stopped the driver from going into Point Road, but despite our every effort in persuading him to keep away from it, the Japanese occupier, being under influence of drink, stubbornly & insistantly ordered driver to drive on. This was however firmly rejected with the result that the Japanese, speaking in some kind of Japanese language supposedly of abusive nature, demanded to know my number, which was being covered by the favour of rain coat worn at the time, then the Japanese grabbed my lanyard in an attempt to loose my tunic button, but, I fearing that the Japanese might snatch the pistol I carried, caught hold of his hand, walking along to the station. C.P.C. 2784 did not point at him with his pistol as alleged, as there was no necessity to use force of arms. The accusation is false and the report should not be believed. C.P.C. 2784 corroborated this statement.
